title: Pure dimension of fibres of a flat family with dense pure-dimensional generic fibre
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that the generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is dense in $X$ and that, for an integer $d\geq0$, every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X_\eta$ has Krull dimension $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then every nonempty fibre $X_s$ is pure of dimension $d$, meaning that each of its irreducible components has dimension $d$. The same holds for every nonempty geometric fibre $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, where $s\in S$ and $\Omega$ is any algebraically closed extension of its residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-fibre-product]. The empty scheme is allowed as $X$, in which case the conclusions are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0GSK, remark-flat-equidimensional, second list, with F=O_X; consequence of Tag 0GSJ, lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional. Geometric fibres: literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex, Tag 02NK, lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d, with relative dimension defined in Tag 02NJ.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and an irreducible component $C$ of $X_s$. Apply the flat generic-component incidence lemma: it supplies a component $B$ of $X_\eta$ with generic point $z$ such that $C$ is a component of $Z_s=\overline{\{z\}}\cap f^{-1}(s)$. Its hypotheses are precisely integrality of $S$ and flatness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 0GSK (remark-flat-equidimensional), second list: reduction to closures of generic-fibre components; affine lifting uses Algebra Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down), algebra.tex.

proof.text: Apply the flat fibre-component-closure dimension lemma to $f$, $t=\eta$, $B,z$, and $C\subseteq Z_s$. It gives $\dim C=\dim B=d$, with the last equality supplied by the generic-fibre hypothesis. Thus all ordinary fibres have the asserted component dimensions. Only $f$ is assumed flat; flatness of the reduced closure is unnecessary.

By locally-finite-type base change, $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is locally of finite type. Apply the pure-open local-dimension lemma to $Y=X_s$, its whole open subset $O=X_s$, and $n=d$. Step 2 supplies every component dimension, so the local topological dimension $\dim_x X_s$ equals $d$ at every $x\in X_s$.

For any algebraically closed extension $\Omega/\kappa(s)$, apply the field-extension component/local-dimension lemma to $Y=X_s$, $k=\kappa(s)$, $L=\Omega$. Its locally finite type hypothesis was checked in step 3. It identifies local dimensions on $G=X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with those on $X_s$ and gives, at each component generic point $z$, $\dim D=\dim_{p(z)}X_s=d$. This proves the geometric-fibre assertion. If a fibre or $X$ is empty there are no components and the assertions are vacuous.
